intro: How your organisation is set up: its name and places, the features that suit your kind of business, how documents are numbered and behave, how the app looks, and the connections to the outside.
start: Check your organisation's name, number and contact details in Organisation. They print on invoices, quotations and emails.
Add each shop, warehouse or office in Locations.
Switch on the industry pack that fits the work at each place.
Go through Document settings with the guided setup, so each document behaves the way you work.

articles.title: Set your organisation's name and details
articles.summary: Your name, registration number and contact details are used on invoices, quotations and emails.

steps.rest: Under Who you are, give the organisation name, its identification number and its industry.

steps.lead: Fill in How to reach you:
steps.rest: the website, email and phone customers should use.
New documents and emails carry them.

tips: The logo, colours and the small print at the foot of documents are set in Studio › Brand.

articles.title: Add a second shop or warehouse
articles.summary: Add a place. Stock, numbers and people can then be kept for each place.

steps.rest: on Locations.

steps.lead: Give it a name and its address.
steps.rest: The address prints on documents made at this place.

steps.lead: Set its currency, language, time zone and date format,
steps.rest: and its working hours, day by day.
The place is listed, and can be chosen on documents, stock and people's access.

articles.title: Switch on the features for your kind of business
articles.summary: An industry pack adds the pages, words and starting settings a kind of business needs, at the places that do that work.

steps.rest: under Add a pack, and press See what it adds.

steps.lead: Choose where it should be on:
steps.rest: every place, only the places you choose, or off everywhere.
it runs at. Each says when it suits the pack.
with the pack's name. Its pages appear in the menu for people at those places.

tips: Turning a pack off hides it and keeps every record.
Where two packs name the same thing differently, choose the word on Your words.
When an update is ready, the pack says so. An update only replaces a setting nobody changed.

articles.title: Verify your business to open wallets
articles.summary: Wallets, receiving accounts, payouts and bill payments open once the business and its directors are checked.

steps.rest: if wallets are not on yet.

steps.lead: Enter the registration (RC) number and press Save the number.
steps.rest: Then press Check with the registry.

steps.lead: See the registered name and directors
steps.rest: filled in for you.
Press Check with BVN or NIN and enter their 11 digits.
from Drive: the registration certificate, identification and proof of address.

tips: In review means a check is with the registry and has not answered. It is not a failure: do not ask again. The page updates by itself.
Needs attention means a check did not match. Read the reason under the item, correct the number or the name, then press Check again.
Once a number has been used for a check, only its last four digits are shown.

articles.title: Set how the app looks for everyone
articles.summary: Choose the brand colour, colour mode, density and font, and which of them people may change for themselves.

steps.rest: or type its code.
It says if text on it would be hard to read.

steps.lead: Turn on People may choose their own
steps.rest: beside the colour mode, density or font you want to leave to each person.
Everyone sees it at once.

articles.title: Change how invoice numbers look
articles.summary: Change the parts of a number and when the count starts again. Numbers already issued keep theirs.

steps.rest: on Number series, such as invoices.
all places, or Add numbers for one place to give a place its own.
Add a part for your own letters, the year, the month or a place code, and move them into order. The preview changes as you type.

steps.lead: Choose when the count starts again:
steps.rest: never, each year, each month or each day.
The next document is numbered the new way.

tips: Numbers already issued do not change. Nothing is renumbered.
A number is never issued twice. A series that starts again each year must show the year in it.

articles.title: Change how a document behaves
articles.summary: Each kind of document is a set of questions: approvals, prices, what it may be made from. Answer them for your business.

steps.rest: or open the kind of document you want to change, or search all the settings.

steps.lead: Read each question in plain words,
steps.rest: with an example from your own answers, and choose. The recommended answer is marked.
Documents follow it from then on.

tips: Start from a preset sets many answers at once. Press See what changes before Apply. Most businesses pick Balanced.
A setting can be set for one place, where it says so. A place follows the organisation for everything it leaves alone.
Changed from the default lists what you changed. Reset takes one back.

articles.title: Choose who gets the weekly digest
articles.summary: The weekly summary of your business goes to your team unless they say no. Choose who, when and what is in it.

steps.lead: Under Who gets it, turn on the roles.
steps.rest: People who join later with them get it too.

steps.lead: Choose the day and the time.
steps.rest: Each person gets it in their own time zone.

tips: Changing the default does not undo the choices people made for themselves.
Milestones are quiet notes when something real happens, like a first sale. They are set beside the digest.

articles.title: Choose who gets each conversation

steps.rest: on Routing, and give it a name.

steps.rest: such as those that come in by a channel or account, or say certain words.

steps.lead: Choose who to give it to:
steps.rest: a person, or a team as a whole, each in turn, or whoever has least open.

steps.rest: if it should change them, then tick In use.
Try it shows which rules a message would meet before it arrives.

tips: Rules run in order. Let the rules after this one add to it lets a later rule add its tags too.
How fast each conversation must be answered is set in Service levels.

articles.title: Join the trading network
articles.summary: Turn the network on, set what partners see about you, and send your documents for verification.

steps.rest: Your business gets a network ID.

steps.lead: Fill in the names and numbers partners see,
steps.rest: your contact and address, and the addresses people can find you by.

steps.lead: Choose the documents you send and accept,
steps.rest: then press Save the profile.
on the verification tab, attach each document asked for, and send it for review.

articles.after: Once verified, other verified businesses can find you and ask to connect. The verified tag is lost if the legal name or a number changes, until it is checked again.
